subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should a sandboxed subagent Docker startup failure remain an accepted asynchronous run that terminalizes visibly, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight the sandbox enough to reject before returning accepted?
rationale: Both choices can fix the silent stall, but they change the public async spawn contract, session/run state semantics, and overlap with the broader lifecycle issue.

options.title: Terminalize async startup failure
options.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` non-blocking and add a typed logged terminal state that `sessions_history`, `subagents list`, and waits can show for Docker startup failures.

options.title: Preflight sandbox before accept
options.body: Validate enough of Docker sandbox startup before returning accepted, trading compatibility and latency for immediate rejection.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle tracker
options.body: Treat this issue as the sandbox-specific proof case while maintainers decide the broader lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

recommendation.title: Terminalize async startup failure
recommendation.body: Keep `sessions_spawn` non-blocking and add a typed logged terminal state that `sessions_history`, `subagents list`, and waits can show for Docker startup failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history trail for `sessions_spawn` sandbox inheritance and gateway accepted semantics points to this owner path.
